docs.title: Siren
docs.text: A modular interface for nanopore raw data analysis.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/satriobio/bulkvis.git
cd bulkvis
git checkout siren
conda env create -f env.yaml

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
First build the image from the dockerfile.

docker build -t pileupy:latest .

Run tool from the image

docker run -it -v $(pwd):/data/ pileupy:latest

docs.title: Basic setup
docs.text:
Start app

siren

Open the app http://localhost:5006/

The app have 3 parts: input pane, tool box, and tool page.

docs.title: Input pane
docs.text: Specifiy input in input pane, use either raw signal file (POD5) or bulk signal file (FAST5). Provide input before select the tool available.

docs.title: Toolbox
docs.text:
Currently Siren has 4 tools available. Click tool icon in tool box to open tool page.

  • Signal visualization
  • Bulk visualization
  • Signal mapping

docs.title: Signal visualization
docs.text: Enter read ID, start, and end time to visualize raw signal. Apply normalization or breakpoint calculation if needed.

docs.title: Bulk signal visualization
docs.text: Enter channel ID, start, and end time to visualize bulk raw signal. Select available annotation if needed.

docs.title: Preparing input
docs.text:
The BAM file should be generated with move tables and MD tags. You can refer to the tutorial below for guidance on how to generate such a BAM file.

dorado basecaller sup pod5/ --emit-moves | \
samtools fastq -T pt,mv,ts - | \
minimap2 -ax map-ont --MD -y ref.mmi - | \
samtools view -hb -F256 | samtools sort - > test.aln.bam

Enter refence file path, contig name, start, and end time to visualize signal mapping to reference.
